findings.evidence: <input id="name-input" name="full_name" type="text" ... required> (line 12, label 'Full name') ... <input id="given-input" name="given_name" ... required><input id="family-input" name="family_name" ... required> (lines 61-63, labels 'First name' / 'Last name')
findings.fix: Collect the name once. Remove either the single 'Full name' field or the split 'First name' / 'Last name' pair, keeping whichever shape the rest of the system needs.
findings.violation: The form asks for the person's name twice: once as a single required 'Full name' field near the top, and again as two further required fields, 'First name' and 'Last name', later in the same form. Both askings are required, so every person filling in the form must supply the same information twice, in two different shapes.

findings.evidence: <input id="member-input" name="membership_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required> ... <input id="acctnum-input" name="account_number" type="text" required>
findings.fix: Drop the membership-number and account-number fields from account creation, or make clear they only apply to an existing member linking a prior account, and make them optional for everyone else.
findings.violation: The form's own heading and submit button ('Set up your account' / 'Create account') frame this as the task of creating a new account, yet it requires both a membership number and an account number before that account exists. A person signing up for the first time has no such numbers to give, so the task cannot use an answer most new sign-ups cannot supply.

findings.fix: Say beside the field what the number is used for, or make it optional.
findings.violation: A phone number is required with no word beside the field on why it is needed, though the form already asks for an email address.

findings.fix: Move the rule into hint text beside the field, linked with aria-describedby.
findings.violation: A format rule appears only in the placeholder, which disappears as soon as typing starts.

findings.fix: Mark the optional fields with the word optional in their labels, or mark the required ones and explain the mark.

instances.evidence: <input id="name-input" name="full_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="password-input" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" required="" minlength="6">
<input id="street-input" name="street_address" type="text" autocomplete="address-line1" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="member-input" name="membership_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">
<input id="given-input" name="given_name" type="text" autocomplete="given-name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="family-input" name="family_name" type="text" autocomplete="family-name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">

findings.violation: The form mixes 14 required and 1 optional fields and marks none of them, so the person cannot tell which may be left empty.
A control that clears everything entered sits directly beside the submit button.

findings.fix: Remove the font-size and padding overrides, or set them so the button renders at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels including padding.
findings.violation: The declared CSS sets this button's font size to 11 pixels with only 1-2 pixels of padding, rendering a control only on the order of 13-15 CSS pixels tall, well under the roughly 44-pixel size mobile-usability guidance recommends and likely under WCAG's 24-pixel conformance floor as well, so a fingertip cannot reliably land on it.

findings.evidence: <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Create account</button> <button id="reset-btn" type="reset">Clear form</button>
findings.fix: Style the primary submit as the visually dominant control (e.g. a filled button) and the reset or clear action as visibly lesser (e.g. a plain text button), so prominence alone signals which one to press.
findings.violation: The secondary action (Clear form) carries no distinguishing style from the primary action (Create account); neither button declares any style, so both render with identical default prominence and the person must read both labels to find the one that saves their entry.

findings.fix: Remove the preferred-contact-time field from account creation, or ask it only at the point a contact is actually being scheduled.
findings.violation: Creating an account does not itself involve anyone contacting the person, so a required answer about when to contact them serves a later step, if any, and could be asked only once that step is reached.

findings.fix: Remove the secondary-phone field from this step, or move it to an optional profile-settings page completed after account creation.
findings.violation: A second, optional phone number has no stated use in creating an account; its answer is not needed now and, if ever needed, could be asked later.

findings.fix: Remove the shipping-speed field from account sign-up, or make it an optional, editable account preference rather than a required field at this step.
findings.violation: Preferred shipping speed is an order-time decision; creating an account does not need it now, and the answer could be collected when the person actually places an order.
This account number is a text field without the numeric input mode, so a phone shows the full keyboard for digits.
